problem: The sentence '6LoWPAN frames (Unit 3) are tiny, so a full OpenFlow header does not fit' is technically wrong as written. An OpenFlow header is only 8 bytes (version, type, length, xid) and fits easily in a 6LoWPAN frame; what does not fit is a complete OpenFlow message carrying a long match specification, together with the per-message overhead and the many round trips needed. A student would wrongly learn that the 8-byte header itself is too big.
fix: Write: '6LoWPAN frames (Unit 3) are tiny, so a full OpenFlow match message, with all its header fields and per-message overhead, does not fit in one frame without fragmentation, which is costly; lightweight southbound protocols are used instead.'
